standard.title: Household Sewing Machines — Feed Bars — Specification (First Revision) (घरेलू सिलाई मशीन — फीड बार — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes raw material classifications, heat-treatment requirements, critical dimensional tolerances, hardness limits, and sampling plans for the manufacture of feed bars used in domestic lockstitch household sewing machines.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes raw material classifications, heat-treatment requirements, critical dimensional tolerances, hardness limits, and sampling plans for the manufacture of feed bars used in domestic lockstitch household sewing machines.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print or stamp the physical 'ISI Mark' standard mark on the feed bar body or protective packaging cardboard to demonstrate conformity to IS 11280.
requirements: Each piece of the feed bar must be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name or registered trademark, country of origin, and type designation.
Feed bars must be designated by the part name ('Feed Bar'), the type, and standard number. For example, a feed bar of Type B is designated as: Feed Bar B IS 11280.
To prevent dust and moisture ingress, each feed bar must be wrapped separately in a sealed polyethylene bag after proper cleaning and dust removal prior to boxing.
Individually wrapped feed bars must be securely packed in outer boxes/cases in accordance with the best prevailing trade practices to prevent mechanical damage or warping during transit.

Lots are inspected for dimensions, tolerances, workmanship, and finish based on standard lot-size tiers (e.g., lot size up to 15 has sample size n=5 with 0 permissible defectives, while lot size 1301 and above has sample size n=125 with 5 permissible defectives).
Hardness testing on forged steel feed bars is conducted on a smaller sample size (e.g., 2 pieces for up to 15, 15 pieces for 1301 and above), and zero failures are permitted to accept the batch.

All observed or calculated physical parameters, hole sizes, and surface hardness numbers must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.
